# ABAP development skills for SAP S/4HANA, SAP ECC, and SAP BTP

Skills for SAP ABAP development across customer-managed and cloud systems: Standard ABAP on SAP ECC 6.0, SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP, and SAP S/4HANA (on premises or on Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud VMs), enhancements and integration, plus ABAP Cloud with RAP and clean core assessments.

Each skill states the SAP products, SAP_BASIS releases, and ABAP development model it targets. Where SAP runs does not change the development model: an ECC system on Azure VMs is still classic ECC with Standard ABAP. Code samples and test answers are parsed offline with abaplint using the grammar of the target release, plus release rules for syntax abaplint accepts too early. That rejects most syntax an older release does not support, but not all of it; docs/sap-environments.md lists the gaps. Activation, ATC results, and runtime behavior still need a real system; see docs/sap-environments.md and docs/testing.md.

## Install

```text
# Claude Code
/plugin marketplace add enterprise-agent-skills/enterprise-agent-skills
/plugin install sap-abap@enterprise-agent-skills

# GitHub Copilot CLI
copilot plugin marketplace add enterprise-agent-skills/enterprise-agent-skills
copilot plugin install sap-abap@enterprise-agent-skills

# OpenAI Codex CLI (the Codex IDE extension does not support plugins)
codex plugin marketplace add enterprise-agent-skills/enterprise-agent-skills
# then enter /plugins in Codex, install sap-abap, and start a new session

# Any Agent Skills compatible agent (Copilot in VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and others)
npx skills add enterprise-agent-skills/enterprise-agent-skills --skill sap-abap-standard
```

Claude Cowork and claude.ai: Customize > Plugins > Add > Add marketplace, then enter `https://github.com/enterprise-agent-skills/enterprise-agent-skills`.

To update:

- Claude Code: run `claude plugin update sap-abap@enterprise-agent-skills` in your shell, or open the plugin on the **Installed** tab of `/plugin` and select **Update now**. Claude Code does not update plugins from this marketplace automatically unless you turn it on: select `enterprise-agent-skills` on the **Marketplaces** tab of `/plugin`, then **Enable auto-update**.
- GitHub Copilot CLI: run `copilot plugin update sap-abap`.
- Claude Cowork and claude.ai: in Customize > Plugins, select **Check for updates**, or turn on **Sync automatically** for this marketplace.
- Skills installed with `npx skills`: run `npx skills update sap-abap-standard`.

## Data and permissions

This plugin bundles the MCP servers below. They start or connect only in agents that support plugin MCP configuration. Review each server's own documentation for the data it accesses.

| Server | Publisher | Transport | Authentication | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SAP system MCP server | Enterprise Agent Skills contributors | stdio | your own credentials for your system | https://github.com/enterprise-agent-skills/enterprise-agent-skills/tree/main/plugins/sap-abap/mcp/sap-system |

The `sap-system` server is published from this repository (`mcp/sap-system/`) and runs on your machine. It needs Python 3.10 or later with the mcp (2.x) and httpx packages (the launcher prints the pip command when they are missing) and network access from your machine to the SAP system's ICM port, for example 44300 for HTTPS or 50000 for the trial's HTTP. It connects only to the SAP URL you configure, with your own SAP user and password, and sends data to no other host. It is read-only, with no setting that turns that off: it blocks every HTTP verb that could change the system, blocks free SQL, validates object names against SAP naming rules, filters WHERE clauses, and limits rows (500 by default). Your credentials never appear in tool results. Prefer an HTTPS URL; use http:// only for a trial system on the same machine.

How each agent gets the connection details (SAP system URL, SAP user, SAP password, SAP client, and logon language):

- Claude Code asks for them when you enable the plugin and keeps the SAP password in its secure credential store.
- Gemini CLI asks for them when the plugin folder is installed as an extension and keeps the SAP password in the system keychain; `gemini extensions config sap-abap` changes them later.
- GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, and other Agent Plugins hosts do not prompt: run `node <plugin folder>/mcp/sap-system/launch.mjs setup` once. It tests the connection and writes the values to `%APPDATA%\enterprise-agent-skills\sap-system.env` on Windows or to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/enterprise-agent-skills/sap-system.env` (by default `~/.config/enterprise-agent-skills/sap-system.env`) elsewhere, outside the plugin folder. Environment variables (`SAP_URL`, `SAP_USER`, `SAP_PASSWORD`, `SAP_CLIENT`, `SAP_LANGUAGE`) take precedence over that file, and `SAP_SYSTEM_MCP_ENV` names a different file.

`<plugin folder>` is the folder your agent installed the plugin to; in a clone of this repository it is `plugins/sap-abap`.

The helper script `skills/sap-clean-core-check/scripts/lookup_api_state.py` downloads a file from SAP's Cloudification Repository on GitHub ([SAP/abap-atc-cr-cv-s4hc](https://github.com/SAP/abap-atc-cr-cv-s4hc), served from raw.githubusercontent.com) each time an agent runs it. The file lists the release state of SAP objects. The script looks up object names in it on your machine and sends no code or object names. To work offline, download the file once and pass `--source <local file>`.
